brief.purpose: find the events and incidents that need follow-up and move them to an owner

direction.rationale: 7 composition hypotheses proposed across 7 families — each pair differs on at least one structural axis of §4.1 (audited: distinct). | The 'select' decision class has no weight table of its own; the 'explore' table is the nearest by task shape (nearest-neighbour mapping, recorded so the scores are auditable). | Selected 'table' (6.28/100) over 6 alternative(s); Chose "table" over "split-view" (6.28 vs 5.84). Gains: taskFit, informationHierarchy, densityScanability. Gives up: none.. | Steering: the planner receives 'table' as its desiredComposition hint, under its own viability rules — the planner may still conclude the roles in play cannot support it.

skills.why: visual-intent.alignment: No readout-dense task; alignment stays loose so the editorial rhythm carries.; visual-intent.alignment overridden: The compiler applied type-and-space's value (No readout-dense task; alignment stays loose so the editorial rhythm carries.). The overridden decision stays here for audit.

archetype: Choosing between options needs the options beside enough detail to choose well. Content shape: 7 information item(s), numeric readouts absent, spatial request not stated.; focal-role: The archetype names what the eye is for, so the plan's focal can be checked against it.; rejected:dashboard: Stated so the composition is a decision, not the absence of one.; visual-intent.density: From the archetype's density rule for this decision figure and content shape; overridden by a composition descriptor when the direction states one.; visual-intent.rhythm: The archetype's whitespace contract; overridden by a composition descriptor when the direction states one.; visual-intent.alignment: Editorial composition breathes: alignment stays loose so the rhythm rests with the content.

discoveries: Type-role contract: the screen name takes the title role, the decision context takes the subtitle, each information item takes its natural role (eyebrow for metadata, label for chrome-ish captions, body for prose, code for identifiers), and status states take the label role at legible size.

Acceptance criteria declared: no label below 11px; uppercase reserved for eyebrows; one spacing rhythm step between sibling regions; body columns around 75 characters. Measured on rendered evidence when screenshot critique runs (issue #22 phase 2).
Composition archetype contract: list-detail (planner runs after this and derives regions; the plan is reviewed against this contract).
Field conflict on 'visual-intent.alignment': 'visual-intent.alignment'='loose' from composition-strategy overridden by type-and-space's decision; overridden decision kept in the trail.
Compiled visual intent (density 'balanced', rhythm 'even', alignment 'loose')  validated against the runtime's schema.
Values on this screen are illustrative, not live telemetry.
The screen avoids generic SaaS card walls and equal-weight panels.
